correctness.rationale: The width-gap proof checks. If a tail of the right anti-diagonal is zero before the terminal 1, the corresponding difference-row entries collapse to a constant, and the next left-edge value |e_i-1|=1 forces e_i∈{0,2}. For a defective sequence, take the rightmost failure e_i>1+B of Muney's interval-completeness inequalities, where B is the tail sum. The suffix is then the full even set {0,2,...,B+1}; B=1 would contradict the zero-suffix lemma, so B>=3. Applying the failing reverse fold gives exactly B+2>=5 positive distances. Every earlier fold contains an injective translate and cannot reduce cardinality; if zero appears for the first time it is an additional point, so the final two-sided extension width is at least 10 (indeed at least 11 in that branch). The equivalence |K_S|<=9 iff A(S)<=7 and the three width-5/7/9 anti-diagonal forms then follow from the candidate-interval size, parity, e_1>0 and the same suffix lemma. I also independently regenerated all sequences through n=9 and found no violation; the repository verifier extends this through n=10 with counts matching OEIS.

originality.rationale: Muney's 2026 paper establishes the corrected reverse-tree theory, the exact interval-completeness criterion, the first hole (2,3,5,9,15), and the exact minimum width. The record targets the next near-minimum regime and gives a sharp defective-width gap plus a complete classification through width nine. Targeted searches for a subsequent near-minimum classification or width-nine solution found no competing result, and the indexed literature still points to Muney as the current source. The exact wording of the source's later open-question section was not independently re-read from full text in this run, so the originality conclusion is based on the source's indexed scope plus the absence of a located follow-up and is explicitly qualified.

scientific_value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp structural gap between interval-complete and defective extension sets and reduces the entire near-minimum regime to the scalar anti-diagonal sum A(S), with exact forms for widths 5,7,9. This materially advances the finite valid-extension problem and provides a reusable rightmost-failure mechanism, while remaining clearly separate from the prime Gilbreath conjecture.

citations.note: Muney, Holes in Valid-Extension Sets of Finite Gilbreath Sequences; source for the corrected reverse-tree theory, first-hole example, interval-completeness criterion, minimum width and enumeration context.
OEIS enumeration for finite increasing Gilbreath sequences; the independently regenerated counts through n=9 and repository counts through n=10 agree.

limitations: The theorem classifies only the near-minimum regime |K_S|<=9; widths 10 and above remain unclassified.
